tool_args.rationale: The supply-bullwhip bridge points to the two-layer siphon law. A saturating term plus a positive square-root term fits the five pilot rows to rounding precision, but all rows have s_grad = 1, so they identify only vmax*(1-rho/2), not vmax and rho separately. The open-branch probe is the least costly way to vary the sink gradient and resolve that ambiguity before confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the positive square-root siphon branch now using the archived sink coefficient
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The branch fits the pilot to rounding precision, but fixing the sink coefficient would assume that inhibition transfers unchanged from the source systems.
It costs more, and the bridge signature and pilot fit favor testing sink dependence before investigating memory dynamics.
